paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Isaiah shows two pictures, and they're both about who gets to be on top. In the first, the mountain of the house of the LORD is "raised above the hills," and many peoples say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD." He will teach them His ways, and they will walk in His paths (Isaiah 2:2-3).

In the second picture, everything we stack up to feel big gets cut down to size. Silver, gold, chariots and idols filled the land, and the LORD is clear that He alone will be exalted (Isaiah 2:7-8, 11). Even the tallest cedars and the strongest walls land on the list (Isaiah 2:13-15). I wear a tall chef's hat and I still got humbled just reading it! Whatever we lean on besides the LORD, the Day of the LORD of Hosts will bring it low (Isaiah 2:12).

So here's why it matters to you, baker. Isaiah ends with "Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils" (Isaiah 2:22). That includes the biggest person you know, and it includes the person in your mirror. But before any of that, Isaiah calls out, "Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD" (Isaiah 2:5). That invitation is still the best news on the page, so let's go up the mountain and let Him teach us.
